answer: I ran the 3-qubit GHZ circuit on sirius:mock with 200 shots. The circuit was H on qubit 0, CNOT 0 to 1, CNOT 1 to 2, then a measurement of all 3 qubits. I sent one job, 01a15f16-5602-73fe-afc3-48ec4c60c0bd, and it finished. The counts were {"000": 200}. A real GHZ state would split roughly evenly between 000 and 111. All 200 shots came back as 000, so this mock backend did not simulate the circuit. It only checks that the job runs end to end. These counts say nothing about real GHZ behavior. The run cost no credits because sirius:mock is free. The script is /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-6/scratch/ghz.py.
